source: Chen, Nai et al., Learning Holistic Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation with a Bipedal Mobile Manipulator (2026), Fig. 2; captions use facts stated in the paper and project page.

steps.label: One target
steps.title: One target from any source
steps.text: VR teleoperation, a learned diffusion policy and scripted trajectories all reduce to one command: a 6-DoF end-effector target in the robot's base frame.

steps.label: Whole body
steps.title: One policy for all 14 joints
steps.text: The actor maps the target and the current observation to position offsets for all 14 arm and leg joints at 50 Hz; no base-velocity, gait or footstep command is given.

steps.label: Context
steps.title: Context from recent history
steps.text: A Transformer reads the last 10 onboard observations and a GRU carries memory across windows; their context z_t tells the actor how the body is responding. Only the estimator and the actor run on the robot.

steps.label: Gated reward
steps.title: Reward gating in simulation
steps.text: In simulation, a phase variable shifts the reward from locomotion and approaching the target toward precise tracking and stabilization; locomotion and manipulation safety scores gate the task rewards.

steps.label: Privileged critic
steps.title: A privileged critic
steps.text: An asymmetric critic sees privileged simulator state such as true base velocity and contact parameters; GAE turns rewards and values into advantages for PPO.

steps.label: Two updates
steps.title: Two kinds of update
steps.text: PPO updates the actor and the critic. The estimator learns only from its auxiliary loss, predicting velocity and the next observation, because its context is detached during PPO updates.
